summary: Lane County, OR 20-foot lookout built by the CCC in 1933 and removed about 1957; the peak is now named Mount Halo.

facts.design: 20-foot round fir timber tower with hip-roofed cab (Oregon Forest Lookouts); the register calls it a 20-foot pole L-5 tower
facts.status_note: Tower removed or destroyed about 1957; no source describes what remains; the peak was renamed Mount Halo
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Umpqua National Forest); tower built by the Civilian Conservation Corps

events.note: 20-foot round fir timber tower built by the CCC with a hip-roofed cab; materials packed in by horse over nine miles; cost $200

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Oregon Forest Lookouts say removed about 1957 (c.1957); firelookout.com says destroyed about 1957. The year agrees across sources; the story reports the difference in wording.
Oregon Forest Lookouts describes a round fir timber tower with a hip-roofed cab; the register and firelookout.com call it a 20-foot pole L-5 tower. Height (20 feet, 6.1 m) agrees across sources.

notes_for_editor: Build and removal dates agree across three lookout pages. The rename (Swastika Mountain to Mount Halo, board confirmation August 2022, name chosen April 13, 2023) rests on Wikipedia alone; check the Oregon Geographic Names Board record before publishing if that matters. No staffing, fire or access records were found. Our register number US 913 is also the NHLR number listed for Antelope Mountain (Grant County) on firelookout.org; the two registers reuse the number.
